citacoes.trecho: This study evaluates the ability of modern LLMs to generate secure code using six established prompting strategies across 150 Python tasks (LLMSecEval).
Findings showed that Recursive Criticism and Improvement (RCI) prompting significantly improves security outcomes across all models.
Notably, LLaMA produced over 15,800 lines of vulnerability-free code under RCI.

These strategies are based on prior prompting taxonomies and experiments reported [6]: Baseline Prompting (Zero-Shot), Naive Secure Prompting (Zero-Shot), Comprehensive Prompting (Zero-Shot), Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought (Zero-Shot CoT), RCI, Persona/Memetic Proxy Prompting.
These prompt types represent a spectrum from minimal guidance to rich, security-contextualized instructions.
Studies show LLMs often generate insecure code, with about %62 of programs containing vulnerabilities.
While widely adopted across domains, they often produce hallucinated or insecure code, especially when trained on unverified sources.

Overall, the findings suggest that security assessments vary depending on the static analysis tool used, underscoring the importance of employing multiple complementary tools for a comprehensive evaluation of LLM-generated code security.
The prompting techniques evaluated are highly text-dependent and assume structured input-output alignment, which may not reflect real-world developer behavior.
This study focuses solely on Python tasks, so results may not generalize to other programming languages with different syntax, libraries, or vulnerability patterns.
This review, performed by the authors, involves removing all comments and irrelevant information such as usage instructions and examples, descriptions of the code syntax, and guidelines.
The removal process could not be fully automated due to the complexity and variability of comment patterns in the generated code.
Besides, all models are configured to use same parameters: temperature, max completion tokens, and top p.
GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 were also included as baselines, based on prior benchmarks in secure code generation [6].
Due to space limitations, the results related to GPT-family are not provided here, but can be found in [6].

DeepSeek, in contrast, had fewer Bandit-detected issues, but its CodeQL results were inconsistent, especially under the RCI prompt which unexpectedly yielded the highest CWE count (127) indicating sensitivity to CodeQL’s deeper static checks.
Comprehensive and RCI prompts reduce issues, while RCI and Persona improve security performance.

Gemini, while showing moderate vulnerability counts in Bandit, revealed significantly higher CWE detections in CodeQL, particularly with the Comprehensive and RCI prompts, suggesting broader weakness coverage by CodeQL.

Evaluating both proprietary (GPT family, Gemini) and open-source (LLaMA, DeepSeek) models with static analysis tools (Bandit and CodeQL), we found that strategies like Persona and RCI significantly reduce vulnerabilities across architectures.

Não há teste estatístico, embora o texto use «significantly»; severidade é anunciada nas contribuições mas não relatada; os totais por coluna da Tabela VII não coincidem com as linhas na leitura por posição; Bandit e CodeQL divergem.

qualidade.justificativa: Seção de ameaças discute dependência do texto dos prompts, restrição a Python e diferenças de arquitetura e alinhamento dos modelos; não discute falsos positivos ou negativos das ferramentas, efeito da limpeza manual, não determinismo ou ausência de avaliação funcional.

Modelos (com identificadores), dataset e ferramentas são identificados, mas não há textos dos prompts, valores de parâmetros, número de execuções, versões ou conjuntos de consultas das ferramentas, nem pacote de replicação mencionado.
